title: UUID under a generic credential name with no provider context
summary: A UUID assigned to a generic credential-like name (api_key, token) in a config with no provider keyword, host or SDK name.
rationale: The bare legacy Heroku key has the UUID shape, but so do many ordinary identifiers. The UUID specification warns that UUIDs must not be used as security capabilities and says nothing about a given value, and no provider statement attributes this value. Family recognition is not established; whether generic credential-name policy should cover a UUID is a separate product decision.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. Missing: a provider statement attributing UUID-shaped values under generic names to a family, or a recorded project decision on generic credential-name handling of UUIDs. Downstream: redact-secret owns action policy; credential-eval and redact-secret-benchmarks own any measurement.

sources.supports: UUIDs must not be used as security capabilities and should not be assumed hard to guess; nothing about any particular value.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
